warning_signal_comment: Revolver is nearly maxed out at 97% drawn and the cash balance dropped below $6M this month. Without sponsor support the company runs out of liquidity within two quarters.
Leverage covenant tripped again this quarter at 5.9x against a 4.0x limit. The bank group is negotiating a waiver with a pricing step-up as a condition.
Sales fell 18% versus last year and the order book keeps shrinking. Management cut guidance for the second time.
The finance chief quit with no successor lined up, the third senior departure this year. Reporting quality is expected to suffer.
Freight rates remain below breakeven across the sector and two peers entered Chapter 11. Fleet utilization stuck near 65%.
Audited statements are now four months late and the auditor flagged revenue recognition issues that may lead to a going concern note.
$180M term loan comes due in under a year with no takeout arranged. Bonds quoted in the low 60s suggest the market doubts a refinance.
The anchor account, roughly a third of revenue, chose not to renew. Pipeline replacement covers under 40% of the loss.
Regulators opened a probe into billing practices and legal reserves were topped up by $22M. New bookings may take a reputational hit.
EBITDA jumped 30% on the back of the restructuring and margins are back to double digits. Revolver fully repaid and undrawn.
Sponsor put in $60M of fresh equity which cured the breach, and the amended facility now matures in 2030. Leverage back under 3x.
Quarter was broadly in line with plan; no covenant issues and liquidity is adequate. Continuing to monitor the sector backdrop.
